newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechens call president, parliament poll on Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: Chechens call president, parliament poll on Jan 27.

text.p: Chechen separatists have called local elections in their region for January 27, Itar-Tass news agency quoted a local official as saying on Friday.

The separatists had said earlier this week that the polls would be held in January. It was not yet clear if Moscow, which insists the Caucasus territory stay part of the Russian Federation, would recognise the election.

Tass quoted separatist Chechen government representative Akhyad Idigov as saying that international observers would be asked to monitor the election, which would choose a president and a parliament for the region.
Representatives of the "opposition" -- the Moscow-backed Chechen government of Doku Zavgayev -- would be invited to join the central electoral commission.
The Russians staged presidential and parliamentary elections in Chechnya last December and June, but neither poll was recognised as valid by international observers or the rebels.
These "elected" authorities were in any case effectively sidelined by the peace deal between Yeltsin's former security adviser Alexander Lebed and the separatists in August.

Interfax news agency quoted a senior official in the self-styled Republic of Ichkeria as saying the separatists were worried about the dismissal of Lebed, accused by President Boris Yeltsin of not playing by the rules.

"Everyone is watching the development of events in Moscow with concern," he said. "The leaders of Ichkeria think that with the dismissal of Lebed, the key factor in the process of peaceful settlement in Chechnya has been removed."

Lebed signed a peace deal on August 31 with Chechen chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov under which Russia promised to pull troops out of the southern region and both sides decided to defer a decision on Chechnya's future status for five years.
The deal ended 21 months of fighting in which tens of thousands of people had been killed.
